items.title: Bobby Militello interviewed by Monk Rowe, Buffalo, New York, October 14, 2002
items.q: Christian McBride was there, Brubeck, ourselves. You do seminars, things, work with the kids and everything...

ctx.x: You know just to wrap up here, I wondered if you can describe what you think of when you solo. What do you take into consideration?

I’ve done some clinics and I’ve sort of come up with a way, an analogy, at clinics to try and get kids into it. I think of nothing. Absolutely nothing. My best solos are in the black spaces. If you’re going to blow — now this I’m going to say — this isn’t unequivocally correct, this is my view. If you’re going to blow a great solo you can’t have analytical thought get in your way. To me, you already have to know the changes and you already have to know what you’re going to do. You have to allow your ears and your…

always look to your left because traffic comes from this direction so you look there first then you look over here. You have all these rules. Try driving the car and thinking about those. You can’t. Try playing golf and trying to think about how you put your hands and what you do and the position of your shoulder and where you — no that’s for when you practice. But when you go to play the game you’re in the zone. When you go to drive the car you’re in the zone. You do it inherently because you’ve practiced enough…
